input.quote: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
input.rationale: Section 7 allocates IP through the Type I / Type II construct. Type I Materials are Customer-owned (§7.b), which matches our preferred position, but the default under §7.a is Type II — so any deliverable IBM does not expressly designate becomes IBM-owned work product. The Type II licence back (§7.c) is irrevocable, worldwide and paid-up, but it is confined to distribution \"within Customer's Enterprise only\" and omits any right to modify, prepare derivative works or sublicense, so it fails the fallback requirement of a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business. There is also no statement that we retain ownership of our Content and data (§11.6 only makes us responsible for Content; §14.18 covers contact data only). Redline flips the default to Type I, broadens the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and adds a Customer Content/data ownership and no-joint-ownership sentence. Note that IBM's retained ownership of the Base Components (§12.1, §12.3) is acceptable and is not disturbed.

proposal.summary: Default deliverables to Customer-owned Type I Materials, broaden the Type II licence to include modification and sublicensing for our business, and confirm we retain ownership of our Content and data.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the work product we pay for, so Materials should default to Type I (Customer-owned) rather than IBM-owned, and the licence to IBM-owned Type II Materials needs to let us modify and sublicense them for our business rather than internal use only. We have also confirmed that our Content and data remain ours, with no assignment to IBM and no joint ownership; if IBM prefers, we can keep IBM's ownership of generic tools and know-how provided the broader licence back stands.

ops.oldText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type II Materials.
ops.newText: If not specified, Materials will be considered Type I Materials.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, and distribute, within Customer's Enterprise only, copies of Type II Materials.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up license to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, distribute, modify and prepare derivative works based on, and sublicense, copies of Type II Materials for Customer's business purposes.

ops.text: e. As between the parties, Customer retains all right, title and interest (including all intellectual property rights) in and to the Content and all other data Customer provides or that is generated for Customer through the Services. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to IBM any ownership of the Content or such data, and no Materials or data will be jointly owned.
